CheckTitle: Ensure no 'root' user account access key exists
Description: The root user account has unrestricted access to all AWS resources. Access keys for the root account must not exist; if compromised, they grant full programmatic control over the account without any MFA barrier.
Risk: Root access keys provide unrestricted programmatic access. A compromised root access key enables full account takeover, including modification of all IAM permissions and deletion of all resources, with no additional authentication barrier.
Remediation: Delete all access keys associated with the root user. Sign in as the root user, open IAM > Security credentials, and remove all root access keys. Use IAM roles for programmatic access instead.
SeverityBasis: AWS Security Hub FSBP IAM.4 (ASFF score 90.0 = CRITICAL); CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v3.0.0 Control 1.4 (Level 1)
AuthoritativeSource: CIS Amazon Web Services Foundations Benchmark v3.0.0; AWS Security Hub FSBP
